lead: the friendships that took hold all started the same way — you went straight at the thing she had not said, on the second evening, and she was either relieved or she never rang you again.
sun: the job was what she was telling you about. what came with it was a bad year folded into the way she said the word manageable, and a brother nobody in that family will name. she had offered none of it. so the going started, and it came out as work: a call made elsewhere, a weekend arranged to read as an ordinary weekend, a difficulty answered before anybody had a term for it.
moon: the appetite goes at the unresolved thing, and nothing about it is dignified — you will drive at night, ask the question nobody asks, be at a door before working out whether you are wanted there. it runs on the difficulty being live. answer the difficulty and it goes quiet inside the same fortnight, on a day you could not afterwards identify.
pull: you appear when something is wrong. all of them have noticed, and the true account — that the trouble itself is what the wanting goes at — is worse than the charge.
tension: she got seven months of somebody who would answer the phone at any hour, and then a friend who is fond and slightly elsewhere, and she has drawn the obvious conclusion about which of the two is real. the arranging did not stop when the interest did; two of those arrangements are still running. what she can count is how often you ring, and the count tells one story cleanly.
cost: somebody four years into a thing they have told nobody is talking about it in a car park by the weekend, because the going here has no waiting period in it and asks nobody's permission. the long dull middle of a recovery gets none of you. the friends still close are the ones whose trouble you never reached the bottom of, and none of that was chosen.

lead: the wedding is four years old now and still gets referred to as the wedding, and what people remember is you turning on a man who had said nothing to you.
sun: what he was doing was audible from the far side of that room and available to nobody else there — the toast pitched half a degree wrong, the joke about her father's house, the beat before he said the word family. you had it at correct weight, and no part of it would hold up if said aloud. it had been running for fifteen years, and for fifteen years you had been answering it quietly.
moon: what came out was sized to the fifteen years rather than to the toast, because nothing here leaves you at a fraction of itself. one sentence, at full weight, in a room with the cake still uncut. it will not be reduced afterwards, walked back, or taken round to two people privately first. the mark sits on that evening permanently, and the evening belonged to somebody else.
pull: the provocation was real, it had lasted fifteen years, and it was inaudible to everyone in that room but the two of you. he has never once looked surprised about it.
tension: her mother rang the following week to ask, kindly, what had got into you, and nothing could be handed over: a toast, a joke, a pause, none of which is an event. temper became the settled account, with drink attached to it by the ones seated furthest from the top table. the man himself has been careful with you since, warmly, in front of people, and everybody reads that as generosity toward a difficult friend.
cost: the arrangement he had run under that family for fifteen years stopped in one minute and has not come back wearing a different complaint. everyone present handles you a little carefully now, at gatherings, in a way they did not before. you are the person who did that at a wedding, and every room you enter from here holds the possibility that you will do it again.

lead: you were gone six years and back inside a weekend, and inside a month his sister, his money and his sleep were being handled again, by you, with neither of you saying anything had restarted.
sun: the six years were not silent at your end. his news kept arriving in other people's voices — a nephew's wedding, a bad autumn nobody named as bad, the tone his brother used for the word settled — and none of it was sent to you on purpose. so you came home current, holding the whole of that stretch at the resolution you always had, including the parts he took to have gone unwitnessed.
moon: the way back was never shut, and that is a fact about you rather than about him. what returned through it was not only you: the whole apparatus came back in the same fortnight — his father on a sunday, the call about the loan, the week moved so nothing lands on him twice. none of it had to be relearned. none of it was requested.
pull: six years apart was the one piece of evidence you have ever produced, and you came home and dismantled it inside a month by making the house work again.
tension: the account he gives now is that you both needed the time and came back better for it, he believes it, and the people who watched it happen have adopted it. correcting it means producing six years of things he never knew were being handled, which arrives as an accusation of having been managed since he was twenty-nine. so his version stands, and his version has the separation as a phase the two of you went through together.
cost: six years out of a household and you have the current state of every person in it by the second evening back, off nobody's account, so nothing has to be explained and nobody has to confess to anything. the reason you went has not been said out loud. it is sitting inside a marriage that is working, being fed by the same week you are running.

lead: ask any of them what you are like and you get warmth, vagueness, and a story about something you once did for them. you could describe each of those people to the sentence.
sun: the resolution at your end is absurd. the state of a marriage comes off the way somebody says the word anyway. you have the exact week a friend stopped coping, and which of two brothers is lying, and nobody handed you any of it. because you hold it in that detail you move on it early, at the right size, which keeps all of it from surfacing as an event.
moon: fourteen stations of road lie between your sun and your moon, and at that spacing every direction from either runs toward the other. the exactness sits at one end and the blur at the other, and neither has ever reached the one that would fix it. nobody drawing on you decides how much first, because nothing about you arrives with a figure on it.
pull: the reading is exact in every direction but one. turn it on yourself and what comes back has no edges, no total, and a number of people quietly eating.
tension: you have been described to strangers a good many times and never once heard yourself given a shape — kind, easy, endlessly there, sentences that would fit forty other people. the end of you that does the actual work has no outline they could get hold of either. so the ones drawing hardest would say, honestly and without malice, that you seem to want for nothing, and they are reporting exactly what is available to them.
cost: the right thing arrives on the right day, in the hands of a person who never had to describe what was wrong, which is close to the rarest service anyone in your life gets offered. the same faculty returns nothing usable about the outflow. amounts get set at the far end, by people working off a blur, and each of them privately thinks the draw has been modest.
